EARLY TEACHERS

At the opening of the first school year, Mr. Halsel was assisted by Miss Georgia Montgomery, as primary teacher, and a desire to prove the methods of advanced education, this early teaching period was one of short duration and with the addition of two more rooms as the school expanded, the actual teaching period was the very high school period with a whole record of students throughout the year. These rooms being very crowded after much discussion[,] the docketing period was one of short duration.

Mrs. Jud[?] Faris was with Studio Music Musio having her lessons outside school hours, and her classes furnished the musical part of the commencement exercises and similar occasions. Mrs. Mattison taught during those very later years from 1878 to 1880, just before the professor, Holland was the younger, was accorded the most careful treatment and his work in the school.

Mr. H. A. (Dick) Halsel, who was one of the advanced students helping for the Ministry, did part-time teaching from 1877 to 1882; and part-time with the College from 1882 to 1889.

Mr. John S. Burnett, 1876 to 1881, taught in the preparatory school.

Two other teachers recalled are Mr. Burke and Mr. Hudson.²⁵

²⁵Information supplied by Mr. W. F. (Fannie Pierce) Beal, Austin, Texas.
